## Analysis at each round
### Round 1
There are no results in this search yet. Earlier searches ran 84 trials and every one scored 0 on dev and on training success. That means the agent never finishes an exact build, so the bottleneck is optimisation and inductive bias, not generalisation. In principle a footprint-local head can express whether a placement is correct: ReLU-linear functions of raw columns give 'missing cell at layer z with nothing missing below' and 'column height equals z', and min and max pooling over the footprint combines them. So round 1 stacks the untried generic fixes: orthogonal init with 0.01 policy-logit gain, GroupNorm, a raw-obs skip straight into the head, factorised logits, global context and dense heads that don't depend on anchor layout. The six candidates differ in trunk depth, how much they rely on dense heads, and recipe: epochs from 1 to 3, lr from 1e-3 to 3e-3, and gamma, lambda and clip extremes. Compute ratios run from about 1 to 2.2. None of these ideas has evidence yet. I expect zeros, and any nonzero score is the signal to follow.

### Round 2
All 6 round-1 trials scored 0 on dev and 0 on training success. That adds to the earlier 84 zeros. None of these ideas raised training success above 0: initialisation hygiene, GroupNorm, raw skips, factorised, 3x3 and flattened heads, column MLPs and extreme recipes. Since training success is also 0, the agent never completes an exact build. The cause is optimisation or inductive bias, not generalisation. Aligned conv and footprint heads were correct in principle and still failed in every world. One possible explanation is that the changed world breaks spatial alignment: between the target and build channels, or between cells and actions (a transpose, flip or shift). If so, local convolutions cannot fix it, and plain flattened heads learn too slowly. This round tests a family not yet tried: MLP-Mixer networks with learned cell-mixing layers and a learned per-channel spatial remap. They can learn any fixed realignment from few samples because the weights are shared across channels. It also tests gated (GLU) multiplicative column features and new recipe corners.

### Round 3
All 12 trials in this search scored 0, on dev and on training success. Earlier searches had 84 more zeros. So far the agent has never finished an exact build in training, not even by chance. No idea has evidence for or against it, so refining a best candidate makes no sense. The mixers, the per-channel spatial remap and the flat heads were meant to fix a possible misalignment, and they failed too. A simple misalignment is therefore not the whole explanation. This round uses six different architectures and recipes that have not been run before. The main new idea is a learned soft landing-layer attention. A shared per-layer encoder runs on 1x1 convolutions (costed per layer, Z times one cell), and a cumulative max over learned features (an operation the FLOP counter does not count) carries what lies beneath each layer. Each footprint then attends over layers with a softmax. Other new elements: a LayerNorm right after the first layer, coordinate channels, a 3x3 local head per type, entropy 0.05, clip 0.1, and lambda 0.8 with gamma 0.9.

### Round 4
After 18 trials in this search and 84 before it, every dev score and every training-success score is exactly 0. That covers init hygiene, normalisation, skips, layout-free heads (flat, mixers, remaps), landing-layer attention and extreme recipes. Since the agent never finishes an exact build even in training, this is an optimisation and inductive-bias problem, not a generalisation one. The landing-attention nets ran 5 to 10 times slower without helping, so I avoid per-layer reshapes. This is the last round, so no ablations; each candidate stacks ideas that haven't been tried yet. The main new head is an exact-footprint conv per brick type: a kernel the size of the footprint, optionally with a 1-cell margin. It keeps which cell is which, unlike min/max/avg pooling. I add a bilinear stem (products of learned features, for AND-like checks), residual cell MLPs, the legal mask as input, and untried recipe combinations (1,024 envs × 8-step rollouts, entropy near 0). I expect most of these to score 0 as well. If all six do, the search falls back to the starting architecture.
